Subject: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment details and next steps

Hi Ken / Sophie —

Great to speak with you this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our call re: LegacyBank's on-prem / air-gapped requirements: 

Summary of needs we heard:
- Fully air-gapped deployment inside bank environment (no outbound internet from inference plane).
- Hardware will live in bank datacenter; primary constraint is single-rack initially, with potential expansion for scoring throughput.
- Strict upgrade windowing (monthly maintenance windows, no live outbound updates).
- Audit & evidence required: SOC2 artifacts, image checksums, signed SBOM, and installation runbooks.

Action items (owner / ETA):
1) We (Redwood) to share our on-prem hardware & network checklist + airgap deployment guide (attachment) — Marissa / Dev — today EOD.
2) LegacyBank to confirm target QPS and peak concurrent tokens so we can size the initial rack (Ken) — by 2026-03-06.
3) Security team to review offline upgrade process and confirm acceptable maintenance windows (Sophie) — by 2026-03-10.
4) If sizing looks good, we’ll provide an initial BOM & procurement options and an optional reserved capacity quote for hybrid burst to hosted in emergencies — Dev — by 2026-03-09.

I've attached the redwood_onprem_req_sheet.pdf and our airgap_deployment_guide_v1.2.pdf for your review.

If anything in the recap is off, please flag. Otherwise, Ken — can you confirm the QPS/token targets and whether you expect multiple racks inside month one?

Thanks,

--

Subject: Re: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment details and next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the docs. Couple clarifications from our side: 

- Initial target: ~200 QPS for short text generation (avg 256 tokens output) during business hours; peak could hit ~400 QPS during batch jobs.
- We expect to start with a single rack (2x 4-GPU nodes) for PoC; if throughput is constrained we can add a second rack in the next quarter.
- Upgrade windows: monthly maintenance window on Saturday 01:00-04:00 local. No inbound/outbound internet allowed from the inference nodes; management plane may be on a separate network that has restricted egress.
- Security team will need the exact offline upgrade procedure plus a checklist of pre/post tests (can Sophie pick this up?).

Can you also confirm whether Redwood supports block-level OS image signatures (we require verification at boot) and how rollback is handled if a private upgrade fails offline?

I'll coordinate procurement for BOM once we have the recommended node specs.

Thanks,
Ken
Ken Moore | Head of Infrastructure
LegacyBank

Subject: Re: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment details and next steps

Hi Ken / Sophie —

Looping in the engineering side — thanks for the targets. A few responses below and a proposed initial node spec for the PoC: 

Answers: 
- Image verification: yes — we produce signed images and provide a signed manifest + SHA256 checksums. We support secure-boot flows; installation includes verification of signatures prior to bringing inference services up.
- Rollback: offline rollback is supported via the installer; we keep prior image artifacts on the admin USB/update bundle for quick rollback. We include health checks that run post-upgrade and, if checks fail, the node boots the previous image automatically. Full rollback requires manual approval from the bank during the maintenance window.

Proposed PoC node (per server):
- 4x NVIDIA A100 40GB equivalent (or the bank's preferred GPU spec)
- 2x Intel Xeon Gold 24C
- 768GB RAM
- 8TB NVMe local for model artifacts and KV cache
- 25GbE redundant NICs, dual power supplies

For a single-rack PoC (2 nodes) this should meet the 200-400 QPS range with room for caching. If you expect heavy concurrent long sequences we recommend 8-GPU nodes or adding a second rack.

Attachments: airgap_deployment_guide_v1.2.pdf (included by Marissa), and I've attached a short install checklist in the shared Drive link.

Next steps we propose:
1) Ken confirms QPS + acceptance of node spec — by 2026-03-06.
2) Sophie reviews the offline upgrade checklist and flags any security gaps — by 2026-03-10.
3) If green, we’ll send a draft BOM + procurement options and an optional reserved capacity addendum for hybrid fallback — by 2026-03-09.

Happy to jump on a quick 30m with your security team next week to walk through the image verification and offline upgrade process.

Thanks,
Dev Patel

Thanks — this is helpful. A few quick asks from security: 

1) Please provide the exact offline upgrade runbook (step-by-step) and the post-upgrade health checks you run. We need that on file for our change management.
2) We’ll need the SBOM and signed image manifest for audit; can you confirm the cadence and how you deliver these for each release?
3) Procurement: please include a line in the BOM for spare NVMe and spare power supplies per rack.

We’re good to proceed with the PoC spec you proposed pending the runbook and manifest cadence. Ken and I will review the materials and get back with any redlines. Sophie (sec) will sync with procurement on vendor approvals.
